metadata.title: How a Quotient Filter Works.
metadata.gate_p: SIGNED 2026-10-25 (post-render approval of the compressed cut)

beats.narration_text: Sawubona — this is Liam, in for Bear. Claude built a quotient filter and quizzed it on a million strangers. Nearly three thousand wrong maybes. Zero wrong nos.

show.event: Greeting 'Sawubona, Liam'; the ask types into the composer
Running indicator, then the three real result lines

props.command: Build a quotient filter in Python, fill it three-quarters full, then ask it about a million keys it has never seen. How often does it lie?

beats.narration_text: To know if you've seen a name, you need only a few bits of it — and where those bits sit says the rest. That's a quotient filter: sometimes a wrong yes, never a wrong no.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'you must store the whole name', reconsiders, corrects to 'you need only a few bits of it'

show.event: Line 1 types: 'To know if you've seen a name,'
Line 2 types the misconception 'you must store the whole name', marked in accent, deleted, retyped as 'you need only a few bits of it'
Line 3 types: 'and where they sit says the rest.'

props.text:
To know if you've seen a name
you must store the whole name
and where they sit says the rest.
props.replacementWords: need only a few bits of it

beats.narration_text: Hash Chen to seven bits and cut them. The top three, the quotient, pick slot two. The bottom four, the remainder, are all the slot stores. The address remembers the rest.

shot.new_visual_element: Chen's 7-bit fingerprint cut into quotient + remainder; the quotient becomes the slot address
shot.visual_intent: SHOW: the split on the real fingerprint of 'Chen' (0100101), evidence worked.inserts[0]

show.event: Quotient bits struck through; slot 2's address 010 ringed

beats.act: Act 2 — WORKED EXAMPLE: store four, ask two
beats.narration_text: Store four names; three bits per slot track who got pushed where. Now ask. Kofi: nobody calls slot seven home — no. Marta: her seven bits match Mei's. Maybe. She was never here.

shot.new_visual_element: Four real inserts with their O/C/S bits; lookup Kofi → NO from one slot; lookup Marta → false-positive MAYBE
shot.visual_intent: SHOW: evidence worked.inserts[3].slots_after and worked.lookups (Kofi, Marta) exactly as the code reported

show.event: Remainders of Chen, Leo, Rosa, Mei drop into slots 2, 3, 4, 6
O/C/S bit rows light exactly as the code left them
Accent chip MAYBE; tag 'never inserted — a false positive'

beats.narration_text: At scale, wrong maybes match the formula: zero point two nine percent. For that error rate, the quotient filter spends twenty-one percent more memory than a Bloom filter. What it buys: one cache line per lookup, not ten.

shot.new_visual_element: Measured false-positive counters vs the typeset formula; +21% bits-per-key bar; 1.09 vs 9.98 cache lines
shot.visual_intent: SHOW: evidence scale block — 2,929 vs predicted 0.292%; Bloom 844; 14.67 vs 12.12 bits/key; 1.09 vs 9.98 lines

show.event: QF counter rolls to 2,929 per million
Cache-line strips: 1.09 lines vs 9.98 lines per lookup

beats.narration_text: Its weak spot: fullness. Half full, a lookup reads one and a half slots. At ninety-five percent, two hundred and fifty.

shot.new_visual_element: Measured slots-per-lookup vs load on a log axis — flat, then a cliff

beats.narration_text: So: the slot is the quotient, the remainder is the record — and never let it fill up.

artifactLines: The quotient picks the slot; only the remainder is stored.
Costs ~21% more memory than a Bloom filter at equal accuracy; reads 1 cache line per lookup, not 10.
Keep it short of full: 1.5 slots per lookup at 50%, 249 at 95%.

beats.narration_text: Your turn: 'Build me an eight-slot quotient filter in Python and find a name it wrongly says maybe to.' Check it shares all seven bits with a stored name. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Build me an 8-slot quotient filter in Python and find a name it wrongly says “maybe” to.
